scenes.narration: There's an animal that survived the vacuum of space. And it's smaller than a grain of sand.
scenes.art: a chubby cute eight-legged tardigrade water bear floating in outer space next to planet Earth, tiny and adorable

scenes.narration: Meet the tardigrade, also called the water bear. The biggest are about one and a half millimeters long.
scenes.art: a cute chubby tardigrade water bear walking on a giant green moss leaf, magnified view with a big magnifying glass frame

scenes.narration: Their superpower? When things get bad, they dry out, curl into a little ball called a tun, and basically pause life.
scenes.art: a cute tardigrade curling up and drying into a small wrinkled barrel shape, sleeping peacefully, a pause symbol glowing above it

scenes.narration: In two thousand seven, scientists sent about three thousand of them into orbit, on the outside of a spacecraft.
scenes.art: a small round satellite capsule orbiting Earth with a tiny box on the outside full of sleeping tardigrades
scenes.cite: ESA FOTON-M3; Jönsson et al., Current Biology 2008

scenes.narration: Twelve days of vacuum and cosmic radiation. Most survived. Some even handled raw solar UV.
scenes.art: tiny dried tardigrades in space being hit by bright beams of sunlight and cosmic rays, glowing shield around them

scenes.narration: And back on Earth, the survivors could still reproduce.
scenes.art: a happy tardigrade mother with a cluster of tiny eggs and baby tardigrades on soft moss

scenes.narration: One of their proteins, called Dsup, even cut X-ray damage in lab-grown human cells by about forty percent.
scenes.art: a glowing protective protein shield wrapping around a twisted DNA strand while x-ray beams bounce off it, scientific lab style

scenes.narration: In twenty nineteen, a lander carrying dried tardigrades crashed into the Moon. So, are there water bears up there now?
scenes.art: a small spacecraft lander crashing onto the grey surface of the Moon with a puff of dust, Earth in the black sky

scenes.narration: To find out, scientists fired them out of a gun.
scenes.art: a cartoon lab gas gun shooting a tiny capsule with a sleeping tardigrade at a sand target, scientist in goggles watching

scenes.narration: They survived hits at about eight hundred meters per second. But that crash was probably too much.
scenes.art: a dramatic slow-motion impact crater on the Moon, a tiny worried tardigrade silhouette near the dust

scenes.narration: So probably no water bears on the Moon. Probably.
scenes.art: the quiet Moon surface at night with a tiny tardigrade-shaped question mark in the dust, Earth glowing above

scenes.narration: Where should we send them next?

post.title: This tiny animal survived space 🐻🚀
post.description:
Tardigrades (water bears) survived 12 days of open space, inspired a protein that protects human cells, and crash-landed on the Moon.

Sources:
Jönsson et al. (2008) Current Biology
Hashimoto et al. (2016) Nature Communications
Traspas & Burchell (2021) Astrobiology
